projects.title: SUBC Submarine Drivetrain
projects.cardSummary: A 2:1 contra-rotating gearbox developed through CAD, calculations, FEA, and machining.
projects.summary: Designed a compact 2:1 straight-bevel gearbox to transfer pilot power to UBC SUBC’s counter-rotating propellers.
projects.goal: Deliver 180 RPM to concentric, counter-rotating shafts while minimizing gearbox mass and maintaining alignment, strength, serviceability, and underwater reliability.
projects.built: Combined AGMA gear calculations, DE-Goodman shaft fatigue analysis, and SolidWorks static FEA to iterate bevel gears and ribbed, pocketed 6061-T6 housing plates for CNC machining.
projects.result: Reduced modeled bottom-plate mass by 38%—from 2.35 lb to 1.45 lb—then manufactured and assembled the four-plate housing, bevel gears, concentric shafts, bearings, bushings, and retainers.
verifiedFacts: Designed a compact 2:1 straight-bevel gearbox for counter-rotating propellers.
Targeted 180 RPM through concentric, counter-rotating output shafts.
Used AGMA bevel-gear stress calculations and DE-Goodman shaft fatigue analysis.
Ran SolidWorks static FEA on the bevel gears and housing plates.
Reduced modeled bottom-plate mass by 38%, from 2.35 lb to 1.45 lb.
Designed the housing around 6061-T6 plates and CNC manufacturing.
Manufactured and assembled the four-plate housing, 1144 carbon-steel bevel gears, concentric shafts, bearings, bushings, and retainers.
Spent 100+ hours modelling the gearbox and housing and completed 30+ structural and flow simulations.
